newsitem.title: JAPAN: Dlr off highs in Tokyo after jumping on trade data.
newsitem.headline: Dlr off highs in Tokyo after jumping on trade data.

text.p: 0320 GMT TRADED HIGH/LOW AS OF 0300 GMT
The dollar was off its earlier highs against the yen by Tokyo midday on Thursday but remained well-supported by short-covering interest and bids from Japanese institutional investors, traders said.
The greenback jumped versus the yen following the release earlier in the day of Japanese customs-cleared trade data for June, which showed a smaller-than-expected surplus.
Japan's trade surplus in June rose 27.7 percent year-on-year to 934.21 billion yen. Economists' forecasts had ranged from 971.0 billion yen to 1.61 trillion yen.
The trade surplus with the United States rose 26.8 percent year-on-year in June to 373.14 billion yen.
Interbank players rushed to cover short positions after the data release and U.S. funds were also detected buying the greenback, traders said.
"The dollar jumped about half a yen shortly after the trade data release as the surplus came in below one trillion yen," said a trader at a long-term bank.
But the dollar was capped by offers from Japanese exporters above 116.20/30 yen, traders said.

"Exporter offers around 116 yen were absorbed, but there are more lined up above 116.50 yen. The dollar's upside looks heavy at around Wednesday's New York high of 116.40 yen for now," said a trader at a trust bank.
Traders said bids from Japanese institutional investors are likely to keep the dollar well-supported.
Japanese investors, who have been selling dollars to hedge risks for their U.S. Treasury holdings, were now eager to unwind those dollar shorts, traders said.
Some Japanese life insurers, however, might consider hedge dollar sales if the dollar climbs above 117 yen, said the long-term bank trader.

U.S. international trade data for May will be released at 1230 GMT on Friday, but traders said the market may be more interested in next week's Humphrey-Hawkins testimony by Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan.
"The market's focus is quickly moving away from the U.S.-Japan trade imbalance. So the U.S. trade data may not move the market unless there is a big surprise," said a trust bank trader.
The dollar remained stuck in a narrow range against the mark due to a lack of fresh incentives, although another rise above 1.80 marks could not be ruled out, traders said.
The German currency rose versus the yen on short-covering, but its upside was capped by offers from automakers, traders said.
The mark stood at 64.77/80 yen, compared with around 64.50 yen in New York on late Wednesday.
The dollar closed at 115.50/60 yen and 1.7910/20 marks in New York on Wednesday.
-- Tokyo Treasury Desk +81-3-3432-9780
